top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a clean, well-understood mechanism (magic-wavelength trapping cancels the light shift for many atoms at once) that was invented by Katori and realised and pushed to 10^-18 by Katori and Ye. It is mature, experimentally verified and opens new tests of gravity, constants and dark matter. The two-laureate allocation is tight and the citation scope is precise, so an award is clearly preferable to no award.
